newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures plunge on BOJ remarks.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures plunge on BOJ remarks.

text.p: Key December three-month Euroyen futures ended Tuesday's TIFFE day session sharply lower after a Bank of Japan (BOJ) official said the market does not always move in line with economic fundamentals.
The December settled at an intraday low of 99.08. Turnover jumped to 94,913 from 28,986 on Monday.
Masayuki Matsushima, director of the BOJ's research and statistics department, said: "The market sometimes overshoots."
Matsushima also said the impact of a planned consumption tax hike on consumer spending may be relatively mild. Japan's three-percent consumption tax will be raised to five percent on April 1.

Matsushima's remarks have prompted some players to speculate that the BOJ may be preparing to end its current stance of allowing the key overnight rate to remain slightly below the 0.5 percent official discount rate (ODR), a trader at a long-term credit bank said.
"If the December dips to 99.00, we can say it has factored in (a possible change in the BOJ stance)," he said.
The December fell below the key technical support level of 99.17 in the morning, following news that a government scheme for improving land liquidity will be announced on March 31.
The key contract extended losses in the afternoon as a large-lot sell order emerged at around 99.16, forcing more players to liquidate longs, traders said.
The key unsecured overnight call rate was slightly higher. Traders predicted Tuesday's weighted average to be 0.49 percent, up from Monday's 0.48 percent.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) injected 200 billion yen into the money market on Tuesday morning, maintaining a neutral stance.
"The overnight rate is likely to continue facing upward pressure until this fund-raising demand before the fiscal year-end eases," a regional bank trader said.
About 220 billion yen worth of three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.55 percent, traders said.
Three-month CDs were last issued on March 11 at a rate of 0.55 percent. They were offered at 0.54 percent on Monday.
One-month CDs were offered at 0.55 percent. Two-month CDs were offered at 0.54 percent. Both rates were flat from Monday.
